transcript.text: Dan, Priya, I've read the draft of your placement report. Let's start with the company. Priya, who did you work for?
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: Before we begin, I should say that we both found the placement much more useful than we expected.
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: I'm glad to hear it. Please make that clear in the introduction.
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: A small logistics firm called Northway. They deliver medical supplies to hospitals.
transcript.speaker: PRIYA

transcript.text: And Dan?
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: An advertising agency, mainly on the social media team. I had thought I'd be doing creative work, but most of the time I analysed engagement figures.
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: Did you have a mentor?
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: Mine was only part-time during the term, but Priya's was full-time in the holidays.
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: Yes, and it was tiring, but it really helped me understand how an organisation works day to day.
transcript.speaker: PRIYA

transcript.text: Yes, a woman called Helen, who'd been there for fifteen years. She let me sit in on client meetings, which I didn't expect.
transcript.speaker: PRIYA

transcript.text: My mentor was so busy I barely saw him. The person who really helped was an intern from the previous year.
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: What was the hardest part?
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: For me it was probably learning to ask questions without feeling embarrassed.
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: That's a valuable lesson. Put it in the reflection section, with an example.
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: Time management. Deliveries are urgent, and I kept underestimating how long tasks take. By week three I was using a planner, and that fixed it.
transcript.speaker: PRIYA

transcript.text: Dan, you mentioned in the draft that you nearly left the placement. Why?
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: It was the repetitive work in the first month. Then they gave me a small campaign of my own, and my attitude changed completely.
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: Good. Priya, what skill do you think employers will value most from your placement?
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: Probably communication. Dealing with anxious hospital staff on the phone taught me to stay calm and explain things clearly.
transcript.speaker: PRIYA

transcript.text: For me it's adaptability. Plans changed daily, and I learnt not to take it personally.
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: Those are good points. Employers often say they want people who can adapt quickly.
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: We looked at some job adverts to check, and nearly all of them mentioned it.
transcript.speaker: PRIYA

transcript.text: In your conclusion, I'd like you to be more critical. At the moment the report is far too positive.
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: We can add a section on the weaknesses, like the lack of training on the software.
transcript.speaker: PRIYA

transcript.text: Exactly. Be specific, and give recommendations to the company.
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: We could also ask our supervisors to write a short comment, if that's allowed.
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: That would be excellent evidence, but they must send it to me directly.
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: Should we send them a copy?
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: Not before I've marked it. The university policy is that reports stay confidential until the grades are published.
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: Fine. When is the deadline?
transcript.speaker: PRIYA

transcript.text: The twelfth of May. Last year some students thought it was the fourteenth and missed it, so check the website.
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE

transcript.text: Got it, thanks.
transcript.speaker: DAN

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms Clarke. We'll make the changes this week.
transcript.speaker: PRIYA

transcript.text: Good. I'm looking forward to reading the next version.
transcript.speaker: MS CLARKE
